ideas.title: Heave! The friends push the empty cart up the dune
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Compared with round 1 this answers the main risk: the cart is general PrintSim parts with Bekker sinkage per cell, foot grip is capped by Mohr-Coulomb shear under each foot's real load, and the friend count comes out of a measured test. That leaves no fitted number and breaks the island's run of devices left alone. The weak spot is still the friends' bodies: if the lean is a pose with a force vector attached and the feet don't really plant, slip and scoop, the shove looks like an invisible hand. The timing key is thin as a game unless the lurch-and-rollback really comes from the ruts.

ideas.title: Sand fences: shape the dune with the wind
ideas.critique: This answers round 1's invisibility problem by running gale-speed saltation live: drifts grow behind fences on screen, streamers come off the crest and wakes form behind bodies. It is the most radical pitch and gives the player authorship over the terrain. A 2D ground flow with wakes from arbitrary obstacles is the hard part: if the wakes come out as painted shadow masks behind each object instead of a solved flow, the drifts become a decal. Its link to the cart is real but indirect.

ideas.title: A kite pulls the generator
ideas.critique: A steerable cloth kite on a rod line through a drum, a back-emf coil and cells is the first flying, player-controlled energy source, and being dragged across the sand is a funny failure that falls out of the physics. It needs a wind field that doesn't exist yet, plus cloth aerodynamics per panel, an XPBD line and a circuit, all in one step. The likely plain version is a kite with a lift coefficient and a charge bar, and it swaps the big goal's windmill for a different machine.

ideas.title: Riding the slip face
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Savage-Hutter avalanching with separate static and dynamic friction angles is new physics that you watch happen, and bodies carried by the flowing layer make it something you can trigger and surf. It risks reading as tipping the island over if the dune doesn't rebuild, and surfing depends on a cart and friends that don't push or ride yet. On its own it is closer to a spectacle than a road step.

ideas.title: Hide and seek by footprints
ideas.critique: Prints pressed in by each creature's real load and gait, then blurred by wind, are an honest way to make the sand readable, and the raking low-sun light suits tracing. Hide and seek is an expected mini game, though, and the hiders' choices will most likely be scripted. Footprint stamping by mass also risks being a decal rather than sand that is really displaced, and it hardly moves the cart forward.
